What is ISO/IEC 42001?
ISO/IEC 42001:2023 is the international standard for artificial intelligence management systems (AIMS). It specifies requirements for establishing, implementing, maintaining, and continually improving how an organization governs the AI it develops, provides, or uses.
Is Dynatrace ISO/IEC 42001 certified?
Yes. Dynatrace LLC holds ISO/IEC 42001:2023 certification issued by Schellman Compliance, LLC, certificate number 1395170-1, effective September 2, 2026, and valid through September 1, 2029.
What is covered by the Dynatrace ISO/IEC 42001 certification?
The certification covers the AI management system supporting the Dynatrace platform, including the AI-powered capabilities developed by Dynatrace and embedded in Dynatrace SaaS and Dynatrace Managed offerings. It covers the people, processes, tools, integrations, and applications involved in developing, deploying, and providing those AI features.
How is ISO/IEC 42001 different from ISO/IEC 27001?
ISO/IEC 27001 addresses information security management. ISO/IEC 42001 addresses AI-specific concerns that security management alone does not cover, such as AI risk and impact assessment, data quality and provenance for AI systems, transparency, and human oversight.
Does the certification mean Dynatrace AI features are certified products?
No. ISO/IEC 42001 certifies Dynatrace's AI management system, not individual products, models, or outputs. The AI management system includes the people, processes, tools, integrations, and applications involved in the development, deployment, and provision of AI features across Dynatrace SaaS and Dynatrace Managed. The standard does not authorize labeling products, processes, or services as ISO/IEC 42001 certified.
Does the certification cover Dynatrace Intelligence?
The certified AI management system covers how Dynatrace develops, deploys, and provides Dynatrace Intelligence, but as explained above ISO/IEC 42001 does not cover specific products.
How can I verify the certification?
The certificate can be verified in the Schellman certificate directory.
How does this help with the EU AI Act and other AI regulations?
Certification is not a statement of conformity with any specific law. It does demonstrate that Dynatrace operates a governed, independently audited AI management system, which supports customers' own diligence and governance obligations when they assess AI in their supply chain.
Where can I learn more about how Dynatrace approaches AI governance?

The end of an earnings season can be a great time to discover new stocks and assess how companies are handling the current business environment. Let's take a look at how Dynatrace (NYSE:DT) and the rest of the cloud monitoring stocks fared in Q2.
Software is eating the world, increasing organizations' reliance on digital-only solutions. As more workloads and applications move to the cloud, the reliability of the underlying cloud infrastructure becomes ever more critical and ever more complex. To solve this challenge, companies and their engineering teams have turned to a range of cloud monitoring tools that provide them with the visibility to troubleshoot issues in real-time.
The 4 cloud monitoring stocks we track reported a strong Q2. As a group, revenues beat analysts' consensus estimates by 2.1% while next quarter's revenue guidance was 0.7% above.
Luckily, cloud monitoring stocks have performed well with share prices up 14.8% on average since the latest earnings results.
With its platform processing over 30 trillion pieces of IT performance data daily, Dynatrace (NYSE:DT) provides an AI-powered platform that helps organizations monitor, secure, and optimize their applications and IT infrastructure across cloud environments.
Dynatrace reported revenues of $554.5 million, up 16.2% year on year. This print exceeded analysts' expectations by 0.9%. Despite the top-line beat, it was still a mixed quarter for the company with an impressive beat of analysts' adjusted operating income estimates but a significant miss of analysts' billings estimates.
Dynatrace delivered the weakest performance against analyst estimates, weakest guidance update, and weakest full-year guidance update of the whole group. Interestingly, the stock is up 29.1% since reporting and currently trades at $59.03.

BOSTON & SAN FRANCISCO, October 01, 2026--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Dynatrace (NYSE: DT), the leading AI-powered observability platform, today announced that it has completed its acquisition of Arize, an AI observability and evaluation platform delivering continual learning for agents.

Bringing evaluation and observability together closes the loop between building AI applications and running them reliably in production, giving teams the visibility they need to catch issues earlier and resolve them faster," said Stephen Elliot, IDC Group VP for Software Development and IT Operations.
"The rise of AI has changed what we need from an observability platform," said Steve Tannock, VP of Platform Engineering Excellence, TELUS. "That's why we're excited about Dynatrace's acquisition of Arize. Together, the two technologies offer a modern approach with real potential to cover the full development lifecycle, from initial build through production."
Arize will continue supporting both Phoenix, its open-source platform, and AX, its enterprise platform. Dynatrace Arize Acquisition Likely Boost AI 'Observability' Growth, UBS Says
Thu, October 1, 2026 at 9:54 AM PDT 1 min read
Dynatrace (DT) could benefit from rising demand for artificial intelligence "observability," with its acquisition of Arize strengthening its competitive position and supporting high-teens annual recurring revenue growth over the next few years, UBS Securities said in a report emailed Thursday.
Checks indicated AI observability could grow to 20% to 25% of total observability spending over the "next few years," potentially adding several percentage points to revenue and ARR growth for Dynatrace and Datadog (DDOG), the report said.
The firm said Arize could contribute $40 million to $50 million of net new ARR in fiscal 2028, while broader adoption of "AI observability" across Dynatrace's installed base could add about 3 to 4 percentage points to revenue and ARR growth in coming years.
UBS said checks with four Fortune 500 Arize customers made it more positive on the AI observability opportunity and the strategic rationale for the acquisition, with all four expecting an aggressive spending ramp over the next several years.
UBS maintained a buy rating on Dynatrace and raised its price target to $74 from $65.

Dynatrace (DT) is being added to the analyst's top picks as the brokerage grows more constructive on the company's AI positioning, sales execution and prospects for revenue and ARR acceleration, Oppenheimer said in a Thursday note.
Oppenheimer said Dynatrace's enterprise customers are ramping AI production workloads, with more than 1,000 now monitoring AI and LLM workloads, while AI customer cohorts are growing 1.5 times faster than non-AI customers, supporting further expansion as adoption increases.
Meanwhile, the company's Arize acquisition adds about 200 basis points to annual recurring revenue growth and expands its AI observability platform, while logs consumption has reached an annualized rate of about $200 million, up from $100 million two quarters ago, according to the note.
Dynatrace's guidance assumes limited AI contribution, leaving potential upside from stronger sales execution and AI adoption, while DPS renewals could also drive net new ARR growth as the product enters its third year, Oppenheimer added.
Oppenheimer maintained its outperform rating on the stock while raising its price target to $71 from $60.

Dynatrace has achieved the international standard certification for AI management systems, ISO/IEC 42001:2023. The certification applies to the AI management systems (AIMS) supporting the Dynatrace platform, including the AI-powered capabilities Dynatrace develops and embeds in Dynatrace SaaS and Dynatrace Managed.
As organizations put AI at the center of how they run, secure, and optimize their software, they need assurance that the AI they depend on is built and operated responsibly. ISO/IEC 42001 is the first international standard to set that bar. It doesn't certify a model or a product claim, but the management system behind them, through the entire development lifecycle. This includes how an organization governs AI, assesses risk and impact, manages the data its AI relies on, and keeps humans accountable for outcomes.
Adopting AI is no longer the hard part. Trusting it is. You need AI that is secure, privacy-preserving, accurate, and risk-managed. And you need more than a vendor's word for it.
AI trust is now part of your procurement conversation, with security, risk, and compliance teams asking harder questions about the AI embedded in the platforms you buy.
Simultaneously, regulatory expectations continue to rise worldwide.
ISO/IEC 42001 certification gives your teams an independent, internationally recognized answer. The AI capabilities in the Dynatrace platform are developed and provided under a governed system, with defined accountability, documented risk and impact assessment, and controls that are audited on an ongoing basis rather than at a single point in time.
For enterprise buyers, particularly in regulated industries, this independent validation provides a concrete trust signal when evaluating AI providers. It can help organizations assess their readiness to adopt AI at scale with governance, accountability, and risk management built into the foundation.
Independent validation of how Dynatrace governs the AI it builds and provides, assessed against a recognized international standard.
Faster due diligence. Certification may help streamline due diligence by providing independently audited evidence for review.
Support for your own AI governance. Certified providers help you demonstrate responsible sourcing of AI within your own management system and regulatory obligations.
Ongoing assurance. The certification is maintained through annual surveillance audits, so it reflects how Dynatrace operates over time.
Achieving ISO/IEC 42001 certification strengthens our approach to governing the AI capabilities we develop and provide.

What is ISO/IEC 42001?
ISO/IEC 42001:2023 is the international standard for artificial intelligence management systems (AIMS). It specifies requirements for establishing, implementing, maintaining, and continually improving how an organization governs the AI it develops, provides, or uses.
Is Dynatrace ISO/IEC 42001 certified?
Yes. Dynatrace LLC holds ISO/IEC 42001:2023 certification issued by Schellman Compliance, LLC, certificate number 1395170-1, effective September 2, 2026, and valid through September 1, 2029.
What is covered by the Dynatrace ISO/IEC 42001 certification?
The certification covers the AI management system supporting the Dynatrace platform, including the AI-powered capabilities developed by Dynatrace and embedded in Dynatrace SaaS and Dynatrace Managed offerings. It covers the people, processes, tools, integrations, and applications involved in developing, deploying, and providing those AI features.
How is ISO/IEC 42001 different from ISO/IEC 27001?
ISO/IEC 27001 addresses information security management. ISO/IEC 42001 addresses AI-specific concerns that security management alone does not cover, such as AI risk and impact assessment, data quality and provenance for AI systems, transparency, and human oversight.
Does the certification mean Dynatrace AI features are certified products?
No. ISO/IEC 42001 certifies Dynatrace's AI management system, not individual products, models, or outputs. The AI management system includes the people, processes, tools, integrations, and applications involved in the development, deployment, and provision of AI features across Dynatrace SaaS and Dynatrace Managed. The standard does not authorize labeling products, processes, or services as ISO/IEC 42001 certified.
Does the certification cover Dynatrace Intelligence?
The certified AI management system covers how Dynatrace develops, deploys, and provides Dynatrace Intelligence, but as explained above ISO/IEC 42001 does not cover specific products.
How can I verify the certification?
The certificate can be verified in the Schellman certificate directory.
How does this help with the EU AI Act and other AI regulations?
Certification is not a statement of conformity with any specific law. It does demonstrate that Dynatrace operates a governed, independently audited AI management system, which supports customers' own diligence and governance obligations when they assess AI in their supply chain.
Where can I learn more about how Dynatrace approaches AI governance?
Visit the Trusted AI page in the Dynatrace Trust Center.
